newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Cisco still busy pre-earnings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Cisco still busy pre-earnings.

text.p: Trading continued heavy in Cisco Systems Inc options ahead of the company's quarterly earnings announcement, scheduled for release after the close of trading Tuesday.
On Monday, traders said the options activity suggested investors were expecting a positive earnings surprise. Implied volatilities were high Monday and remained so Tuesday.
Volatilities in the May 50 and 55 puts were in the low to mid-70's Tuesday and crept up to the upper 70's Tuesday afternoon.
The stock was down a point at 57-7/8 late Tuesday.
Cisco was the most active stock, with turnover of 17.5 million shares.
Among the options, the May 60 call was most active, with total turnover of roughly 8,045 contracts. The May 65 call traded 3,845 and the May 55 call traded 3,965.
On the put side, the May 55 traded more than 5,000 and the May 60 traded 2,400, rounding out the most active.
According to First Call, analysts' consensus estimate for Cisco's third quarter profit is $0.52 a share, up from $0.37 a year ago.
Cisco options trade on the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) and the Pacific Exchange (PCX), with most volume crossing on the CBOE.
Elsewhere, a reverse conversion, or reversal spread in Coca-Cola Co crossed around 3,000 times.
The Coca-Cola June 60 call and put each traded around 3,050 contracts and the June 65 call and put traded 2,275 and 2,890 contracts, respectively.
In other trading, long term options known as LEAPS continued to trade heavily, led by January 1998 options on American Depositary Receipts of Telebras.
The Telebras January 1998 95 and 115 put each traded 10,000 contracts. The 95 put had open interest of 1,551 and the 115 put had open interest of 328.
Telebras shares continued their rally, gaining 3-1/4 to 118-1/8 in late trade.
Also, several January 1999 puts on shares of Homestake Mining were active.
The January 1999 10, 15 and 17-1/2 put each traded 3,300 contracts.
